abstract_snippet: We present an algebraic treatment of exception handlers and, more generally, introduce handlers for other computational effects representable by an algebraic theory. These include nondeterminism, interactive I/O, concurrency, state, time, and combinations. The computation monad is the free-model monad of the theory. Each handler corresponds to a model of the theory. The handling construct is interpreted using the homomorphism induced by the universal property of the free model.
what_the_paper_supports: Algebraic effect handlers: a unified mathematical framework for handling computational effects (exceptions, nondeterminism, I/O, concurrency, state, time) via algebraic theories. Key insight: handling a computation = composing with a unique homomorphism from the free model to a programmer-defined model, induced by the universal property. Handlers are dual to algebraic operations (constructors vs deconstructors). Formalized in call-by-push-value calculus. Denotational semantics via free-model monads. Examples span exception handling, stream redirection, CCS renaming/hiding, timeout, rollback.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: No implementation in a programming language (theoretical paper). No execution trace in the computational sense — effect handlers are semantic, not trace-based. No versioning (GAP-019). No SMT or machine-checked verification (GAP-020). No composition of multiple handler systems beyond theory combination. No practical performance evaluation. Parallel handling left as open question.
paper_core_claims: Handlers for arbitrary algebraic effects, not just exceptions
Handling = composition with unique homomorphism from free model (universal property)
Handlers are dual to algebraic operations: constructors vs deconstructors
Formalized in call-by-push-value calculus with denotational semantics
Generalizes exception handling, stream redirection, CCS renaming/hiding, timeout, rollback
Computation monad = free-model monad of the algebraic theory

GAP-015.reason: Algebraic theories as specification of effects: operations + equations define the effect theory. Handlers specify how effects are handled. This is a formal specification language for computational effects, but not for programs in general.

GAP-016.reason: Free model construction as compilation: effect theory → free model → handler. But this is semantic compilation, not program compilation.

GAP-017.reason: Universal property provides formal equivalence: handler = unique homomorphism. This is a mathematically grounded equivalence between handlers and models. But it's category-theoretic, not behavioral.

GAP-018.reason: Effect operations as intermediate state: operations represent computation state at effect occurrence. Handler interprets operations recursively. This is a form of execution state tracking via algebraic operations — each operation is a state transition point.

GAP-019.reason: No versioning of handlers or theories.

GAP-020.reason: Denotational semantics provides mathematical correctness. But no machine-checked verification.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Algebraic theories as effect specification: operations + equations. Handler language as handling specification. But specification is for effects, not for programs in general.

N2_Representation.reason: Free model as representation of computations. Operations as representation of effect occurrences. Call-by-push-value calculus as formal representation. Handler as representation of effect interpretation.

N3_Compiler.reason: Free model construction as semantic compilation: theory → free model monad. Handler application as semantic compilation: computation + handler → result. But this is denotational, not operational compilation.

N4_Artifact.reason: Handlers are reusable artifacts that can be applied to different computations. But no registry, versioning, or composition mechanism.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Handlers ARE interpreters: they interpret effect operations into computations. The handler language defines how effects are interpreted. The handling construct applies an interpreter (handler) to a computation. This is the most mathematically grounded interpretation model in the batch — handlers are literally homomorphisms (interpreters) from the free model to a programmer-defined model.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Effect operations form a tree (free model element) that the handler traverses recursively. This is a structured execution trace: each operation is a node, handler processes them in order. The computation tree IS an execution trace. But it's denotational, not operational.

N7_Validator.reason: Denotational semantics provides mathematical correctness basis. Equational theory provides laws that must be satisfied. But no machine-checked verification.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Handlers compose: different handlers for different effects can be combined (theory combination). Handler application is a form of routing: computation → appropriate handler. But composition is informal — left as future work for combinations of handlers.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Theoretical paper — no implementation in a programming language
Parallel handling (e.g., CCS parallel operators, UNIX pipe) left as open question
Combination of handlers (not just theories) left as future work
Continuations are NOT algebraic — excluded from the framework
Recursion handling sketched but not fully developed
Type-theoretic approach to limiting well-typed handlers left as future work
